name: Watermelon
description: Water-rich summer melon, eaten chilled.

histamine.note: Fine for most; SIGHI flags it as a mild liberator.

name: Cantaloupe / muskmelon
description: Fragrant orange-fleshed summer melon.

histamine.note: Generally well tolerated fresh.

name: Honeydew melon
description: Pale green, very sweet melon.

histamine.note: Generally well tolerated fresh.

name: Mango
description: The king of fruits; sweet, rich summer stone fruit.

tcm.note: TCM leans cool/neutral — the opposite of the desi view.

ayurveda.note: Ripe mango is called cooling by some schools, heating by others.

unani.note: Classic garam-taseer fruit in desi/Unani usage.

histamine.note: Usually tolerated; occasional reports of flares.

name: Banana
description: Everyday sweet fruit, filling and portable.

histamine.note: Riper bananas are more of a liberator.

name: Apple
description: Crisp everyday fruit, sweet-tart.

histamine.note: One of the safest fruits for histamine.

name: Pear
description: Juicy, grainy-sweet fruit; TCM's classic lung-moistener.

histamine.note: Very well tolerated.

name: Orange
description: Sweet-sour citrus staple.

ayurveda.note: Sour taste reads as heating in Ayurveda.

unani.note: Citrus is classically cold in Unani.

histamine.note: Citrus is a classic histamine liberator.

name: Mandarin / kinnow
description: Easy-peel small citrus.

tcm.note: The dried peel (chen pi) is warm — the flesh is not.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator, like orange.

name: Lemon
description: Sour citrus used for juice, dressing, and sharbat.

ayurveda.note: Sour = heating classically, yet lemon water is widely used as a cooler.

histamine.note: Mild liberator; small amounts fine for many.

name: Lime
description: Small sharp citrus, the desi 'nimbu' in most kitchens.

ayurveda.note: Same sour paradox as lemon.

histamine.note: Mild liberator.

name: Grapefruit
description: Large bitter-sour citrus.

ayurveda.note: Sour-bitter; schools disagree.

histamine.note: Also interacts with many medications (non-histamine caution).

name: Pomegranate
description: Jewel-seeded fruit prized across all four traditions.

tcm.note: TCM leans warm — opposite of the Ayurvedic/Unani view.

ayurveda.note: A classic pitta-pacifying fruit.

histamine.note: Generally well tolerated; sparse formal data.

name: Grapes
description: Sweet table fruit, green or red.

histamine.note: Fresh grapes fine for most; darker/overripe slightly worse.

name: Dates
description: Dense sweet palm fruit; daily staple in Arab and desi homes.

histamine.note: Dried fruit; usually fine unsulfured.

name: Figs
description: Soft honeyed fruit, fresh or dried.

ayurveda.note: Fresh figs cooling; dried more building.

unani.note: Anjeer is garam in Unani texts.

histamine.note: Dried figs (sulfured) worse than fresh.

name: Papaya
description: Soft orange tropical fruit with digestive enzymes.

tcm.note: Thin classical documentation; classical 'mu gua' is actually quince.

ayurveda.note: Classic garam fruit — traditionally avoided in pregnancy.

histamine.note: Papain is a recognized liberator.

name: Pineapple
description: Sweet-sharp tropical fruit.

ayurveda.note: Ripe sweet pineapple called cooling by some.

histamine.note: Bromelain is a strong liberator.

name: Guava
description: Fragrant firm fruit eaten with chaat masala across South Asia.

unani.note: Commonly called thanda in desi usage.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Lychee
description: Perfumed white-fleshed summer fruit.

tcm.note: Famous in TCM for causing 'heatiness' when overeaten.

histamine.note: Sparse data; usually fine in moderation.

name: Longan
description: Small translucent fruit; a TCM blood tonic.

ayurveda.note: Not classically documented; inferred.

histamine.note: Sparse data.

name: Jackfruit
description: Huge fibrous fruit; ripe is sweet, raw is cooked as sabzi.

ayurveda.note: Heavy; schools split on ripe vs raw.

histamine.note: Sparse data.

name: Coconut (fresh)
description: White flesh of the mature coconut.

ayurveda.note: Classic pitta-cooling food.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Strawberry
description: Sweet red berry.

histamine.note: A classic liberator — common flare trigger.

name: Blueberry
description: Small antioxidant-rich berry.

tcm.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: One of the safer berries.

name: Raspberry
description: Tart red berry.

tcm.note: The dried herb is warm; fresh fruit thinly documented.

histamine.note: Moderate amounts usually fine.

name: Cherry
description: Sweet stone fruit of early summer.

histamine.note: Usually fine in moderation.

name: Peach
description: Fuzzy sweet summer stone fruit.

histamine.note: Well tolerated by most.

name: Apricot
description: Small golden stone fruit; dried khubani is a desi staple.

histamine.note: Dried (sulfured) apricots are worse than fresh.

name: Plum
description: Tart-sweet stone fruit.

ayurveda.note: Sweet plums cooling, sour plums heating.

unani.note: Aloo bukhara is a classic cooling sharbat base.

histamine.note: Fresh plums well tolerated.

name: Kiwi
description: Tangy green-fleshed fruit.

histamine.note: Liberator; also a true allergen for some (separate from histamine).

name: Persimmon
description: Honey-sweet autumn fruit.

tcm.note: TCM warns against overeating on an empty stomach.

histamine.note: Sparse data.

name: Tamarind
description: Sour brown pod pulp used in chutneys and drinks.

tcm.note: Thin classical documentation.

ayurveda.note: Strongly sour = ushna.

unani.note: Tamr hindi is used in cooling sharbats — opposite of the Ayurvedic read.

histamine.note: Usually fine in chutney quantities.

name: Avocado
description: Creamy green fruit eaten as a savory.

tcm.note: Not classical; modern TCM sources lean cool-moistening.

histamine.note: High in biogenic amines — a common stealth trigger.

name: Cranberry
description: Very tart berry, mostly consumed dried or as juice.

tcm.note: Not classical; inferred.

ayurveda.note: Astringent-sour; schools would split.

histamine.note: Dried/juiced forms often sweetened and sulfured.

name: Raisins
description: Dried grapes; kitchen and dessert staple.

ayurveda.note: Munakka is a classic cooling-building dried fruit — unusual for a dried fruit.

unani.note: Kishmish leans garam in desi usage — disagrees with Ayurveda.

histamine.note: Dried fruit + sulfites; unsulfured is better.

name: Prunes / dried plums
description: Dried plums, stewed into desi qormas and eaten for digestion.

unani.note: Aloo bukhara is a classic Unani cooler.

histamine.note: Dried fruit; sulfites common.

name: Dragon fruit
description: Mild speckle-fleshed cactus fruit.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: Well tolerated; sparse data.

name: Chikoo / sapodilla
description: Malty brown-sugar-sweet soft fruit.

tcm.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: Sparse data; usually fine.

name: Custard apple
description: Creamy segmented sweet fruit.

tcm.note: Thin documentation.

ayurveda.note: Sitaphal literally reads 'cold fruit'.

histamine.note: Sparse data; usually fine.

name: Mulberry
description: Delicate sweet berry of early summer.

tcm.note: Sang shen is a classic yin-nourishing cold fruit.

unani.note: Shahtoot sharbat is a traditional throat-cooler.

histamine.note: Sparse data.

name: Amla
description: Sour green gooseberry — the one sour fruit the traditions call cooling.

tcm.note: Outside the Chinese record; placed from its sour-astringent character.

ayurveda.note: The textbook exception: amla is amla-rasa (sour) yet shita virya, and the only rasayana that pacifies all three doshas.

unani.note: Aamla is barid-yabis in Unani, a standard ingredient of cooling and blood-purifying formulas.

histamine.note: Not itself on the SIGHI list; sour fruits generally sit low-to-middling.

nutrition.highlight: one of the densest vitamin C sources

name: Red date (jujube)
description: The wrinkled red date dropped into Chinese soups and tonics.

tcm.note: Da zao is a core warming tonic — added to soups to build qi and blood, and to soften harsh herbs.

ayurveda.note: The Chinese species is not the Ayurvedic badari; read across with caution.

unani.note: Unnab in Unani is a cooling demulcent for the chest — the opposite reading to TCM's warming tonic.

histamine.note: Dried but unsulphured in its usual form.

name: Goji berry
description: Small red dried berry, scattered into congee, soups and tea.

tcm.note: Gou qi zi is classically neutral — a liver and kidney yin tonic that suits both hot and cold constitutions.

ayurveda.note: No classical Ayurvedic entry; placed from its yin-nourishing character.

histamine.note: Dried fruit; low, though commercial packs vary.

name: Olives
description: Cured and brined — inedibly bitter straight off the tree.

tcm.note: The Chinese olive is a different fruit; the Mediterranean one has no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; salt-cured and oily reads ushna.

unani.note: Zaytoon and its oil are har-ratab in Unani — warming and moistening, a standard tonic.

histamine.note: SIGHI treats unfermented olives as risky and pickled or fermented ones as worse — table olives are cured, so the curing is what rates them, not the fruit.

name: Pomelo
description: The largest citrus — thick pith, mild flesh, less sharp than grapefruit.

tcm.note: You zi clears heat and transforms phlegm; the peel is used warm, the flesh is cold.

ayurveda.note: Sweet-sour citrus, shita.

unani.note: Thanda like the rest of the citrus family.

histamine.note: Citrus, so a liberator like lemon and orange.

name: Sweet lime
description: The juice-stall citrus — sweet, barely acidic, handed over in a glass.

tcm.note: Not separately classified; read with the citrus family.

ayurveda.note: Sweeter and far less sour than lemon, so shita without the heating sourness.

unani.note: Mosambi is firmly thanda in desi usage — the standard convalescent juice.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator, though milder than lemon.

name: Passion fruit
description: Wrinkled shell, intensely tart pulp and crunchy seeds.

tcm.note: A new-world fruit with no classical entry; placed from its sour-cooling character.

ayurveda.note: No classical record; read as a sour tropical fruit.

histamine.note: Sharply acidic tropical fruit — the same family of triggers as pineapple and papaya.

name: Star fruit
description: Crisp and tart, cut into stars. People with kidney disease are advised to avoid it entirely.

tcm.note: Yang tao clears heat and generates fluids — a summer fruit in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Regional rather than classical; sour-astringent and read as shita.

unani.note: Not part of the classical Unani record.

histamine.note: Low on histamine — its documented hazard is oxalate and neurotoxin load in kidney disease, which is a separate matter.

name: Durian
description: Custard-rich, pungent, and the fruit most famously said to overheat you.

tcm.note: The classic shang huo fruit — eating too much is said to bring on heat signs, and mangosteen is the traditional antidote.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record, but its richness and pungency read ushna.

unani.note: No Unani entry; placed by analogy to rich, oily fruits.

histamine.note: Strong-smelling but not fermented — the smell is sulphur compounds, not histamine.

name: Mangosteen
description: White segments in a thick purple rind — durian's traditional counterweight.

tcm.note: Paired with durian in Chinese and Southeast Asian practice: the cooling queen against the heating king.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; sweet-astringent and read as shita.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Rambutan
description: Lychee's hairy cousin — sweet, floral, slightly firmer.

tcm.note: Grouped with lychee and longan, which are warm and said to be heating in quantity.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; read with the lychee family.

histamine.note: Low, like lychee.

name: Loquat
description: Small orange spring fruit — the one the cough syrup is named after.

tcm.note: Pi pa moistens the lung and stops cough; pipa gao syrup is built on the leaf and fruit.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; read from its moistening, cough-easing use.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Quince
description: Hard, astringent and inedible raw — cooked into jams and stews.

tcm.note: Not a classical Chinese food fruit.

ayurveda.note: Bihi appears in regional use rather than the core texts; astringent and read as shita.

unani.note: Safarjal is well documented in Unani as barid-yabis, astringent, and strengthening to the stomach.

histamine.note: Low; almost always cooked.

name: Blackberry
description: Dark, seedy hedgerow berry, sweet at the edge of tart.

tcm.note: Not classically listed; read with the berry family.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; sweet-astringent.

histamine.note: Better tolerated than strawberry, which is the berry SIGHI singles out.

name: Carob
description: Dried pod ground into a sweet powder — chocolate's caffeine-free stand-in.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; sweet-astringent.

unani.note: Kharrub is documented in Unani as cold and astringent, used for loose stools — the reverse of chocolate's reading.

histamine.note: Low, and specifically the substitute recommended in place of cocoa.

name: Plantain
description: Starchy cooking banana — fried, boiled or curried, never eaten raw.

tcm.note: Read with banana, which is cold; cooking tempers it.

ayurveda.note: Kachcha kela is shita and grahi (binding) — used for loose motions where ripe banana is not.

unani.note: Thanda and drying, unlike the ripe fruit which is thanda-tar.

histamine.note: Carries banana's liberator flag; the starchier unripe fruit is usually better tolerated.

name: Black currant
description: Intensely tart dark berry, more often drunk as cordial than eaten.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Low as fresh fruit; the sweetened cordials are a different question.

name: Ber
description: Small crisp winter fruit sold by the bagful from roadside carts.

tcm.note: A different species from the Chinese red date, though related — read with caution.

ayurveda.note: Ripe badari is sweet and shita; the unripe sour fruit is read the other way.

unani.note: Unnab-family, thanda, used as a chest demulcent.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Phalsa
description: Tiny purple summer berry, crushed into sherbet against the heat.

tcm.note: Absent from the Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: Parusaka is classically shita and specifically a summer thirst-quencher.

unani.note: Falsa sharbat is a standard Unani cooler, prescribed against loo and burning urination.

histamine.note: Low; a short season and eaten fresh.

name: Bael
description: Hard-shelled temple fruit whose pulp is beaten into a summer sherbet.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Bilva is a classical digestive: the ripe fruit is shita and laxative, while the unripe is the opposite — heating and binding.

unani.note: The ripe pulp is thanda, given as sherbet through the hot months.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Soursop
description: Spiny green fruit with soft, tart, custard-like flesh.

tcm.note: A new-world fruit with no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; sour-sweet and read as shita.

histamine.note: Low, though tart tropical fruits vary between people.

name: Kumquat
description: Thumb-sized citrus eaten whole — sweet skin, sharp flesh.

tcm.note: Jin ju regulates qi and resolves phlegm; unusually for citrus, it is read as warm rather than cool.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; the aromatic peel reads ushna.

histamine.note: Citrus, so flagged as a liberator.

name: Cactus pear
description: Desert fruit under a spined skin — mild, seedy, eaten cold.

tcm.note: Not part of the Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

unani.note: Tin shawki is treated as thanda in Levantine and North African usage — a summer fruit.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Green mango
description: Unripe and mouth-puckeringly sour — the base of aam panna, chutney and pickle.

tcm.note: Sour unripe fruit; the Chinese record covers the ripe mango only.

ayurveda.note: Unripe mango is amla-rasa and ushna — classically said to aggravate pitta and rakta, the opposite of the ripe fruit.

unani.note: Desi usage is emphatic the other way: aam panna is the standard drink given against loo and heatstroke.

histamine.note: Sharply sour and usually pickled or salted, both of which push it up.

name: Jamun
description: Deep purple monsoon fruit that stains the tongue, long tied to blood sugar.

tcm.note: Absent from the Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: Jambu is classically shita, kashaya (astringent) and grahi — the seed powder is a standard prameha (diabetes) remedy.

unani.note: Thanda and astringent in Unani usage, given for loose stools and excess thirst.

histamine.note: Low; a short monsoon season, eaten fresh with salt.

nutrition.highlight: the monsoon fruit tied to blood sugar

name: Kokum
description: Dark sour rind from the Konkan coast, soaked for sol kadhi and curries.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Vrikshamla is one of the few sour dravyas classed as shita, and is given specifically against heat and thirst.

unani.note: Thanda and astringent; the coastal summer drink is built on it.

histamine.note: Very sour, so flagged with the other sour fruits, though it is used in small amounts.

name: Cape gooseberry
description: Small golden berry in a papery husk — sweet with a tomato-ish tang.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: Regional rather than classical.

histamine.note: Low, though it is a nightshade — a separate sensitivity from histamine.

name: Dried figs
description: Figs dried to chewy sweetness — soaked overnight and eaten through winter.

tcm.note: Drying concentrates and warms; the fresh fruit is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Drying turns the fresh fruit's shita — anjeer is a winter, building food.

unani.note: Anjeer is har-ratab in Unani, soaked overnight and taken as a winter tonic and laxative.

histamine.note: Dried fruit — concentrated, and commonly sulphured, which is why the dried sits well above the fresh.

name: Dried apricot
description: Apricots dried to leather — Hunza-style, or bright orange from sulphur.

tcm.note: Concentrated by drying; fresh apricot is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Follows the fresh fruit's ushna reading, intensified by drying.

unani.note: Garam, and a standard winter dried fruit alongside anjeer and chuhara.

histamine.note: Dried and usually sulphited — the bright orange ones especially. The brown unsulphured kind is easier.

name: Dried dates
description: Hard dried dates — boiled into winter milk, not eaten soft like the fresh kind.

tcm.note: Dried and concentrated, in the warming dried-fruit group.

ayurveda.note: Building and ushna; taken through cold months and after childbirth.

unani.note: Chuhara is textbook garam in desi Unani usage — boiled in milk as a winter strengthener.

histamine.note: Dried fruit, so concentrated — above the softer fresh dates.

name: Hawthorn
description: Tart red berry sold as sugared strings and simmered into digestive teas.

tcm.note: Shan zha is warm and the classical drug for food stagnation — specifically for undigested meat and fat.

ayurveda.note: No classical Ayurvedic entry; sour-sweet and read as ushna.

histamine.note: Sour fruit, so flagged with the others; used in small amounts.

name: Monk fruit
description: Dried gourd-fruit brewed for coughs, and now sold as a zero-calorie sweetener.

tcm.note: Luo han guo is cool, moistens the lung and stops cough — a standard dry-throat remedy.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; read from its moistening use.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Barberry
description: Tiny scarlet sour berries scattered over Persian rice.

tcm.note: Not classically listed as a food; the related root is a cold, bitter drug.

ayurveda.note: Daruharidra family — tikta and shita, used for liver heat.

unani.note: Zereshk is barid-yabis in Unani, given for bilious complaints.

histamine.note: Sharply sour and dried — flagged with the other sour dried fruits.

name: Sour cherry
description: Sharp red cherries too tart to eat raw — stewed, dried or drunk as sharbat.

tcm.note: Sour and fluid-generating; cooler than the sweet cherry.

ayurveda.note: Shita and sour — a summer sharbat fruit.

unani.note: Thanda; albaloo sharbat is a standard Levantine and Persian cooler.

histamine.note: Sour stone fruit, and usually preserved in syrup or dried.

name: Dried longan
description: Longan flesh dried to a dark chewy raisin — dropped into tonic soups.

tcm.note: Long yan rou is warm and a classical blood and shen tonic, taken for poor sleep and worry.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; sweet and concentrated, read as ushna.

histamine.note: Dried fruit, concentrated — sits with raisins rather than with fresh longan.

name: Dried persimmon
description: Persimmons dried until a white bloom of natural sugar forms on the skin.

tcm.note: Follows persimmon, which is cold; drying tempers it toward cool.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; astringent and read as shita.

unani.note: Placed with the drying dried fruits.

histamine.note: Dried and concentrated.

name: Gooseberry
description: Translucent green berries, sharp enough that they are almost always cooked.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: Distinct from amla despite the shared English name; read as shita.

histamine.note: Sour berry.

name: Redcurrant
description: Strings of translucent red berries, tart and full of seeds.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Sour berry, like its black cousin.

name: Elderberry
description: Dark clustered berries, cooked into syrup — never eaten raw.

tcm.note: The related plant is used for wind-damp; the berry has no clear food classification.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Usually taken as a concentrated syrup, which is where the rating comes from. Raw berries are mildly toxic — a separate matter.

name: Sea buckthorn
description: Intensely sour orange berries from high cold deserts — Ladakh and the Tibetan plateau.

tcm.note: Sha ji is warm and used for cough and blood stasis in the Chinese materia.

ayurveda.note: Regional rather than classical; sour and read as ushna.

histamine.note: Very sour and usually taken as juice or concentrate.

name: Rhubarb
description: Sour red stalks stewed with sugar — the leaves are poisonous and never eaten.

tcm.note: Da huang is cold and strongly purgative in TCM; the culinary stalk is the mild end of a serious drug.

ayurveda.note: Revatchini is shita and laxative in the Ayurvedic record.

unani.note: Rewand is barid and a classical purgative.

histamine.note: Very sour and oxalate-rich; the oxalate is a separate hazard from histamine.

name: Nectarine
description: A peach without the fuzz — the same fruit, one gene apart.

tcm.note: Read with peach, which is warm and generates fluids.

ayurveda.note: Follows the peach: ushna and said to aggravate pitta in quantity.

histamine.note: Low, like peach.

name: Blood orange
description: Orange with crimson flesh — sweeter and less acidic than the common kind.

tcm.note: Read with orange, which is cool and fluid-generating.

ayurveda.note: Follows orange: sour-sweet and classically ushna.

unani.note: Santra is thanda in desi usage.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator, like orange.

name: Yuzu
description: Knobbly aromatic citrus used for its peel and juice, almost never eaten whole.

tcm.note: Aromatic citrus peel is warm and qi-moving in the Chinese reading, unlike the cool flesh.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; aromatic and read as ushna.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator; used in small amounts.

name: Calamansi
description: Small round sour citrus squeezed over everything in Southeast Asian cooking.

tcm.note: Read with the small citrus — cool and fluid-generating.

ayurveda.note: Sour and read as ushna; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Buddha's hand
description: A citron that grows in finger-like segments — all peel, almost no flesh.

tcm.note: Fo shou is warm and one of the standard qi-regulating drugs, used for a tight chest and poor appetite.

ayurveda.note: No classical Ayurvedic entry.

histamine.note: Citrus peel; used in slivers.

name: Aam papad
description: Mango pulp dried in sheets into a chewy sweet-sour slab.

tcm.note: Follows mango; drying concentrates it.

ayurveda.note: Ripe mango is ushna and drying intensifies it.

unani.note: Garam-tar, as aam is in desi usage.

histamine.note: Dried and concentrated fruit, usually with added sugar and salt.

name: Desiccated coconut
description: Coconut flesh grated and dried — the baking and mithai staple.

tcm.note: Read with coconut; no classical Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Narikela is shita and guru; drying does not change its virya.

histamine.note: Low; it goes rancid quietly, which is a fat problem rather than a histamine one.

name: Dried currants
description: Tiny dark dried grapes — smaller and sharper than raisins.

tcm.note: Read with raisins, which TCM treats as warm.

ayurveda.note: Draksha is shita even dried — the classical exception among dried fruits.

unani.note: Kishmish is garam-tar in desi usage, soaked overnight in winter.

histamine.note: Dried fruit, concentrated — with raisins and prunes.

name: Dried cranberry
description: Cranberries dried with a great deal of added sugar, because they are inedible otherwise.

tcm.note: Follows cranberry; a new-world fruit with no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: No classical record.

histamine.note: Dried, sweetened and sour — several contributors at once.

name: Jam
description: Fruit boiled with sugar until it sets — the toast standard.

tcm.note: A preparation rather than a food; the fruit and sugar pull opposite ways.

ayurveda.note: Long boiling with sugar is ushna, whatever the fruit underneath.

unani.note: Garam-tar; murabba is a warming preserve in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Cooked-down fruit with a long shelf life; strawberry and citrus versions carry their own flags.

name: Marmalade
description: Bitter-orange jam with the peel left in.

tcm.note: Citrus base with sugar; peel is warmer than flesh.

ayurveda.note: Sour, bitter and boiled with sugar — ushna.

histamine.note: Citrus with the peel, concentrated by boiling.

name: Apple sauce
description: Apples cooked down soft and smooth — the first food for many babies.

tcm.note: Follows apple, which is cool and generates fluids; cooking warms it slightly.

ayurveda.note: Shita and light; stewing makes it easier again.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, and gentle on a weak stomach.

histamine.note: Low — one of the safer processed fruit products.

name: Canned peaches
description: Halved peaches in sugar syrup — the tin in every store cupboard.

tcm.note: Read with peach; the syrup adds sweetness and damp.

ayurveda.note: Follows the peach's ushna, plus the sugar.

histamine.note: Low — heat-sterilised in the tin, which keeps it down.

name: Tamarillo
description: Egg-shaped tart fruit with tomato-like flesh, eaten scooped from the skin.

tcm.note: A new-world fruit; read with the nightshades, which are cooling.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: A nightshade like tomato, and tomato is one of the highest fresh foods on the SIGHI list.

nutrition.highlight: a tomato that grows on a tree

name: Rose apple
description: Crisp watery bell-shaped fruit with almost no flavour beyond a faint rose scent.

tcm.note: Lian wu is cool and generates fluids — a summer thirst fruit.

ayurveda.note: Shita and light; mostly water.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Karonda
description: Small sharply sour berries, pickled green or eaten ripe and purple.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Shita and astringent; used against bilious heat.

histamine.note: Sour, and usually pickled.

name: Bilimbi
description: Intensely sour green fruit, far too sharp to eat raw — used as a souring agent.

tcm.note: Related to star fruit; read as cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita, though the sourness is ushna by taste.

histamine.note: Extremely sour — among the sharpest souring agents in the set.

name: Mahua
description: Sweet fleshy tribal-forest flowers, dried and eaten or distilled into liquor.

tcm.note: No Chinese entry; sweet and heavy.

ayurveda.note: Madhura and ushna; a building forest food.

histamine.note: Dried and often fermented for liquor — the dried flower alone is moderate.

name: Cherimoya
description: Green scaled fruit with white custardy flesh — sweeter and smoother than sitaphal.

tcm.note: A new-world fruit; read with the custard apples.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Feijoa
description: Aromatic green fruit tasting of guava and pineapple at once, scooped from the skin.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Sharply aromatic and acidic.

name: Medlar
description: Only edible once bletted — left to soften almost to rot before eating.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: Astringent; no classical entry.

unani.note: Zu'rur appears in the Unani record as cold and astringent.

histamine.note: Eaten deliberately over-ripe, which is exactly what raises amines.

name: Salak
description: Reddish scaled skin over crisp segments — sweet, sour and faintly astringent.

tcm.note: No classical Chinese entry despite the region.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Ackee
description: Cooked as a vegetable, and genuinely poisonous unless picked fully ripe and open.

tcm.note: No classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Oily and read as ushna.

histamine.note: Low for histamine. Unripe ackee causes hypoglycaemic poisoning — a serious hazard, and a separate one.

name: Noni
description: Pungent fruit taken as juice for its reputation rather than its taste.

tcm.note: The related root is warming; the fruit is thinly documented.

ayurveda.note: Regional rather than classical.

histamine.note: Usually consumed as a fermented juice, which is what rates it.

name: Tangelo
description: A mandarin-grapefruit cross with a distinctive knob at the stem.

tcm.note: Read with the citrus.

ayurveda.note: Sour-sweet, ushna like other citrus.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Seville orange
description: Too bitter and sour to eat — the marmalade and cooking orange.

tcm.note: Zhi shi, the immature bitter orange, is a standard qi-moving drug; the fruit is cool.

ayurveda.note: Sour and ushna.

unani.note: Narangi is thanda-khushk in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Very sour citrus.

name: Citron
description: Thick-pithed citrus grown for peel and fragrance, with almost no juice.

tcm.note: Xiang yuan is warm and regulates qi — the peel is the medicine.

ayurveda.note: Aromatic and ushna.

unani.note: Turanj is garam in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Citrus, used as peel.

name: White currant
description: A paler, sweeter mutation of the redcurrant.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Sour berry, like its red form.

name: Lingonberry
description: Small tart northern berry, almost always cooked into a sharp preserve.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Sour, and usually eaten as sweetened preserve.

name: Cloudberry
description: Amber arctic berry with a musky, almost fermented sweetness.

tcm.note: Not classically listed.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Low fresh.

name: Black sapote
description: Green outside, dark brown inside, with a texture like chocolate mousse.

tcm.note: A new-world fruit; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: No classical record.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Mamey sapote
description: Dense orange flesh with a sweet almond-and-pumpkin flavour.

tcm.note: No classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Sweet and heavy; read as ushna.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Horned melon
description: Spiked orange shell over green jelly seeds — mild, and mostly a curiosity.

tcm.note: Read with the melons, which are cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita, with the cucurbits.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Ugli fruit
description: A wrinkled loose-skinned citrus, sweeter than grapefruit and easier to peel.

tcm.note: Read with the citrus.

ayurveda.note: Sour-sweet, ushna.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Mikan
description: Loose-skinned winter mandarin, peeled with one hand under a kotatsu.

tcm.note: Read with mandarin; cool and fluid-generating.

ayurveda.note: Sour-sweet citrus, ushna in the classical reading.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Nashi pear
description: Round crisp pear with the texture of an apple and far more juice.

tcm.note: Li is cool, moistens the lung and stops dry cough — a standard autumn fruit.

ayurveda.note: Shita and moistening.

histamine.note: Low.

nutrition.highlight: an apple's crunch, a pear's juice

name: Kaki
description: Firm sweet persimmon eaten crisp like an apple, skin and all.

tcm.note: Shi zi is cold and clears heat; classically not eaten on an empty stomach.

ayurveda.note: Shita and astringent.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Sudachi
description: Small green citrus squeezed over grilled fish — sharper and greener than lime.

tcm.note: Read with the small sour citrus.

ayurveda.note: Sour and ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with citrus.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Kabosu
description: Round green citrus, milder than sudachi, used for its juice rather than its zest.

tcm.note: Read with the sour citrus.

ayurveda.note: Sour and ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with citrus.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Umeboshi
description: Ume fruit salted and sun-dried for months into something intensely sour and salty.

tcm.note: Salted, soured and dried; warming and astringent.

ayurveda.note: Amla plus lavana plus a long cure — firmly ushna.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; taken in tiny amounts as a digestive.

histamine.note: Months of salt fermentation on an intensely sour fruit — high on both counts, though eaten one at a time.
